title: Writing Apprenticeship-Ready OJT Contracts and Cohort Training Plans
description: California has no state OJT directive, and no local OJT template we found is built for a multi-year apprenticeship. This hands-on workshop teaches staff to write an OJT contract and a cohort training plan that fit apprenticeship: hours scaled to occupation, wage steps, reimbursement rates, the 90 percent small-employer waiver, combining OJT and ITA funds, employer documentation, and invoicing. Learners leave with a completed contract package and CCC's template toolkit.
notes: Audience: Case managers, business services, OJT coordinators. Format: FD or CO (with template toolkit). Hours assumed from format (flagship FD/CO workshop = 12 hours). Gap addressed: Board OJT policies vary sharply (San Francisco 50 percent and $6,000; Orange County up to 90 percent and $20,000); Washington's 2026 evaluation names OJT rules that don't fit apprenticeship timelines as a design gap.
learning_objectives: Determine the appropriate reimbursement rate (50, 75, or 90 percent) and document the justifying factors under 20 CFR 680.730 and WSD25-03.
Build a cohort training plan that covers multiple apprentices under one contract.
Set training duration and hours using occupation complexity and the apprenticeship's work process schedule.
Combine OJT and ITA funding for one apprentice without overlap.
Specify the employer records, invoices, and monitoring visits required to close the contract cleanly.
prerequisites: Working knowledge of WIOA Title I eligibility (FND 102 or equivalent)

lessons.title: Project: Build a Complete Contract Package

sequencing_rationale: Lessons follow the catalog's learning objectives in the order a practitioner meets them on the job: Reimbursement Rates and Justifying Factors; The Cohort Training Plan; Setting Duration and Hours from the Work Process Schedule; Combining OJT and ITA Without Overlap; Employer Records, Invoicing, and Monitoring Visits. The closing project ("Project: Build a Complete Contract Package") applies the earlier lessons to one realistic work product (a completed OJT contract package and cohort training plan for a sample apprenticeship, with justified rates, hours, funding split, and closeout records) rather than introducing new content. Scope assumptions: hours are not stated in the source catalog and are assumed from the delivery format (FD or CO (with template toolkit); flagship FD/CO workshop = 12 hours). Content is grounded in California and federal guidance named in the catalog description and objectives; the course cites those directives by number but does not reproduce their text, and every policy-specific claim must be checked against the current directive before delivery. Local board policy is treated as a variable the learner fills in from their own board, not something the course prescribes. Design driver (catalog "gap addressed"): Board OJT policies vary sharply (San Francisco 50 percent and $6,000; Orange County up to 90 percent and $20,000); Washington's 2026 evaluation names OJT rules that don't fit apprenticeship timelines as a design gap. Statistics and audit findings quoted from the catalog have not been independently verified. Prerequisites reflect track order: APP 101 (Registered Apprenticeship for Workforce Professionals); Working knowledge of WIOA Title I eligibility (FND 102 or equivalent).
